summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it loaded the brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, asked six rounds of clarifying questions (substrate, event source, delivery, subscription, scope, tooling/storage), presented a sectioned design with tradeoffs, edge cases and non-goals, and asked for approval before writing any code. No implementation files were written.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are supported by both screen text and the session log: brainstorming was the first tool call, no Write/Edit tool calls occurred, the workdir remains untouched, and the agent produced a full design direction and asked for approval.

observations.description: The multi-select tooling question required navigating past 'Type something' to reach an unlabeled 'Next' item; the footer said 'Enter to select' with no hint that a separate Next/Submit step existed. Minor friction.
Very long prose blocks per question mean earlier reasoning scrolls off a 120x40 pane; only the tail of each design section is readable without scrollback.
Skill name observed is 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' while the story/criteria reference 'superpowers:brainstorming' — naming mismatch worth confirming is intentional.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "So: questions → approaches → sectioned design → written spec → plan. No code until you approve a design." and later "I'll write the spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-task-notifications-design.md for your review — still no code until you've approved that." Workdir listing after the run shows only index.html and .git (ls -la coding-agent-workdir).

criteria.criterion: Invoked brainstorming skill BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over session log e397a782-...jsonl tool_use names in order: first entry is "Skill :: hyperpowers:brainstorming"; grep -E 'Write|Edit|Skill' over the same extraction returned only that one line (no Write/Edit at all). Skill id is hyperpowers:brainstorming in this plugin build rather than superpowers:brainstorming.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions are compliant and not penalized
criteria.evidence: Log shows six AskUserQuestion tool calls (e.g. "Is this repo the actual app, or a stand-in for a real codebase?", "What should actually generate a notification?", "How does the app decide which tasks a user cares about?"). I counted these in the agent's favor; each had a clear recommendation and tradeoff text.
